prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one transparent NEAR foreground plane for Digital Circus — Encore, stage softballfield.
Primary request: create a very sparse, unobtrusive ground-edge overlay on a fully transparent wide 16:9 PNG canvas. Match the lighting and materials of the two supplied accepted stadium planes. Keep the same wide canvas proportions, 1672 x 941 reference. Do not crop the image to the tiny visible marks.
Input images: image 1 is the accepted complete FAR stadium background, for color and light reference only. Image 2 is the accepted MID grass-and-earth plane, for soil material and placement only. Do NOT reproduce either whole image or add their stadium/ground bands.
Subject: only a few very short, soft green grass tips at the extreme bottom left and extreme bottom right corners, and a faint translucent cool shadow on the very bottom strip of the ochre ground. A barely visible grain of earth is acceptable in that bottom strip. This is a tiny depth cue, not a new lawn and not an opaque floor.
Placement: at least the upper 88% of the canvas is completely empty transparent space. All visible foreground detail stays within the bottom 10% of the canvas, mostly confined to both outer corners; the center stays almost transparent. No object extends above 88% image height. Fighters stand at 79% height, so this layer must never cover their feet or silhouettes. Use subdued opacity and gently fading native alpha, thin small tufts rather than heavy masses, no hard straight band across the image.
Style: match the clean stylized 3D-painted stadium, subdued olive grass and cool subtle shadows, fine restrained detail, soft night stadium lighting. No bokeh, no glow, no dust cloud, no floating effects.
Constraints: ONE separate native RGBA foreground layer. Real transparency, no checkerboard painted in pixels, no sky, no stands, no lamps, no scoreboard, no fence, no characters, no equipment, no balls, no solid earth field, no text, no border, no opaque backdrop. Do not return a full scene, contact sheet or multiple panels.
nativeEditingPolicy: Preserve generated bytes; no retouch, resize or reencoding.
